spark.byteSummary:
Understand Transformer self-attention, BPE tokenization, KV-cache memory math, prefill vs. decode bottlenecks, and production serving.

LLMs split text into subword tokens (BPE), project them into embeddings with positional encodings (RoPE), and predict the next token via stacked causal Transformer blocks.

Engineering LLMs in production means balancing context size, quantization, continuous batching, and prompt-caching economics.

```python
# KV-Cache memory estimation per token across all layers (Python)
def kv_cache_bytes_per_token(layers: int, kv_heads: int, head_dim: int, bytes_per_elem: int = 2) -> int:
    # 2 tensors (Key + Value) per layer
    return 2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * bytes_per_elem
```

tabbedExplorer.name: PagedAttention
tabbedExplorer.title: Virtual-Memory Paging for KV Cache
tabbedExplorer.desc: Splits each sequence's KV cache into non-contiguous fixed-size blocks (pages) instead of pre-allocating max_seq_len.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Eliminates internal/external KV fragmentation and enables copy-on-write prefix sharing.

tabbedExplorer.name: Speculative Decoding
tabbedExplorer.title: Draft-Model Verify in One Forward Pass
tabbedExplorer.desc: A tiny draft model proposes K tokens, and the target LLM verifies all K in parallel in a single pass—exact same output distribution.
tabbedExplorer.rule: Turns memory-bound sequential decode into compute-bound parallel verification.

qaDetails.summary: Why are output tokens typically 3x–5x more expensive than input tokens?
qaDetails.body: Input tokens run in parallel during Prefill with high GPU arithmetic intensity, whereas each output token requires a full sequential memory-bandwidth-bound Decode step.

qaDetails.summary: How does Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) shrink the KV cache?
qaDetails.body: Multiple query heads share a smaller number of Key/Value heads, reducing KV-cache size and HBM bandwidth proportionally without hurting accuracy.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which bottleneck dominates autoregressive token generation (Decode) in modern LLMs?

options.feedback: Compute FLOPs dominate Prefill, not single-token Decode.

options.text: B. GPU HBM memory bandwidth (reading weights & KV cache per token)
options.feedback: Correct! Generating one token at a time reads model weights and KV cache from HBM for minimal FLOPs.
Tokenization is microseconds compared to millisecond GPU forward passes.

tipsAndTricks: Monitor TTFT (Time To First Token) and TPOT (Time Per Output Token) separately—they have completely different bottlenecks.
Keep static system instructions and few-shot examples at the very front of the prompt to maximize KV prefix cache hits.
Enforce JSON Schema / constrained decoding for tool calls and downstream parsers rather than regex-parsing freeform text.
